Information received since the June meeting points to a strong labor market, robust real GDP growth, and inflation near the symmetric 2% objective. In standard New Keynesian frameworks with sticky prices and credible targets, this mix justifies a Taylor-type feedback path of “further gradual” rate increases while keeping expectations anchored; at the same time, literature highlights that higher policy rates have a contractionary impact on investment and aggregate demand (including via financial accelerator channels), which tempers the otherwise upbeat signal. Net tone: positive but moderated by expected tightening.
